Prologue

Let's start with the end of the world, why don't we? Get it over with and move on to more interesting things.

First, a personal ending. There is a thing she will think of as the start, though she will be wrong. History did not begin that morning, nor did it end when she found her three-year-old son beaten to death on the living room floor.

His name was Uche. He was small for his age, with solemn dark eyes and thick curls that tangled into knots when he slept. He did not cry when he died.

Now for the continental ending. This is the Stillness, which is not still at all. It is a continent that shivers and grumbles like an old man with indigestion, plagued by earthquakes and acid rains and boiling geysers and toxic clouds.

A season is what ordinary people call a winter, or a summer. But in the Stillness, a Season with a capital S is something else entirely: a catastrophe that blacks out the sun for centuries, choking the air with ash and turning empires into dust.

This is the way the world ends. For the last time.
